title: Customer Admission SLA & Rapid-Response Playbook for Strategic Accounts
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem: Rapid ad-hoc requests from top accounts and escalations are currently funneled through multiple owners (CS, SE, Product) with inconsistent SLAs. This causes unclear commitments, delayed prioritization decisions, and downstream engineering context gaps.

Goal: Define and operationalize a single 'Customer Admission SLA' playbook that standardizes intake, triage, SLA targets, routing, and acceptance criteria for requests that may influence the public roadmap. The playbook should: 1) reduce decision time for VIP escalations to <= 3 business days; 2) ensure transparent commitments (yes/no/deferred) to customers; 3) produce an auditable trail and ticket that maps to roadmap lanes; and 4) provide clear engineering inputs (impact, effort, security/compliance flags).

Scope: Strategic accounts (ARR > $250k), named escalations from Strategic AMs, and legal/compliance requests with product impact. Excludes low-touch feature requests and internal ops items.

Core components to deliver: 
- Intake form template (CS/AM) with required fields (customer impact, use case, SLA, confidentiality level, example prompts/data).
- Triage rubric and scoring (impact, frequency, strategic alignment, technical risk, revenue runway) with numerical thresholds for auto-accept / requires-review / reject.
- SLA matrix mapping request priority to response windows and decision owner (PM lead, Design, Eng IC/Manager).
- Roadmap admission artifact: standardized PRD/one-pager template and ticket metadata mapping to roadmap lanes (Commit / Evaluate / Backlog / Out of Scope).
- Communication playbook: customer response templates (accept/deflect/defer) and internal follow-up tasks (eng estimate request, security review kick-off).
- Instrumentation: dashboards to measure time-to-decision, acceptance rate, downstream implementation latency and revenue retention correlation.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Intake form published in Confluence + CS shortcuts in Intercom within two weeks of ship.
- Triage rubric validated with three pilot accounts and adjusted for edge-cases.
- SLA matrix agreed by GTM, Product, and Eng leadership and published.
- Dashboard with: average time-to-decision, percent of VIP requests resulting in roadmap commits, and closed-loop customer notifications.

Stakeholders: 
- Product: Asha Raman (owner), Marcus Hill (assignee)
- GTM: Sarah Li (Strategic AM lead), Javier Ortega (CS)
- Engineering: Priya Kapoor (runtime), Daniel Reeves (reliability)
- Design: Elena Park (supporting comms/PRD templates)
- Security/Compliance: Marco Silva (advisory)

Trade-offs & open decisions: 
- Threshold for automatic admission vs human review (propose revenue + technical delta scoring).
- Whether admission decisions automatically reserve Dedicated capacity or only inform capacity planning.
- Visibility level: public roadmap note vs private customer commit. Needs legal guidance for forward-looking language.

Implementation plan & timeline: 
- Week 0-1: Draft intake form and triage rubric; align with CS and AMs. (Owner: PM)
- Week 2: Pilot with 3 strategic accounts and collect feedback. (Owner: GTM/PM)
- Week 3: Finalize SLA matrix and templates; create Confluence + Intercom snippets. (Owner: PM/Design)
- Week 4: Build dashboard queries and flag events in ticketing system (Linear tags + Segment events). (Owner: Eng/Analytics)
- Week 5: Rollout to all Strategic AMs; training + office hours. (Owner: GTM/Product)

Monitoring & metrics: 
- Primary: median time-to-decision for VIP requests (target <= 3 business days).
- Secondary: percent of VIP requests with a roadmap commitment within 60 days; NPS change among piloted accounts; number of SLA breaches and root-cause trends.

Related artifacts & links: 
- Draft PRD template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/strategic-admission/prd-template 
- Pilot intake form (Draft): https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1VIP-draft 
- Slack playbook channel: #vip-intake-playbook 
- Example GH PR for dashboard events: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/214

Notes: prioritize low-friction CS integrations (Intercom macros, Confluence templates) before heavy engineering automation. Reserve engineering effort only for dashboard/event plumbing and tagging flows. If triage rubric demonstrates >30% of requests are auto-accept, we will propose a follow-up to define guardrails for capacity reservation and Dedicated allocation.
